proposition: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, the sum of k^2 for k = 1..n equals n(n+1)(2n+1)/6.
hypotheses: the sum is empty for n = 0

argument.text: At n = 1, the sum of k^2 for k = 1..n = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, n^3 + n is congruent to (n^3 + n) + 1265 modulo 55.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, at least one of the following holds: n mod 4 = 0; n mod 4 = 1; n mod 4 = 2; n mod 4 = 3.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, (n-3)*(n^2) equals (n-3)*((n^2) + [n = 3]).
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, if (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0 then n mod 4 = 0.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, n^3 + n is congruent to (n^3 + n) + 2717 modulo 11.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 40 for which n^2 > 13.
The steps above establish the statement up to 40, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 40.
